dimensions.label: Problem Clarity
dimensions.evidence: The workflow scout traced that voice samples reach agents as 220-character excerpts only when hand-picked, never on the dashboard path, and that no style, register, channel, framework or PRODUCT.md material reaches any prompt, while Article.slug and labels derive from the raw idea.

dimensions.label: Goal Definition
dimensions.evidence: Eight pass/fail goals (frozen canon in every input, one lint rule per tagged mechanical rule, framework selection, golden-set drift thresholds, one idea yielding a flagship, kit and siblings, Admin canon editing, owner acceptance of three real ideas, an edit-distance baseline) were proposed and accepted with explicit thresholds.

dimensions.label: Success Criteria
dimensions.evidence: Every goal maps to a named Pest file on the Postgres suite, a grep, or a jq recomputation over recorded evidence; owner voice acceptance, the PRODUCT.md reconciliation and the rendered board review remain explicit judgment calls with mechanical twins where evidence is recorded.

dimensions.label: Scope Boundaries
dimensions.evidence: The owner set the MVP line (data model, canon, frameworks, lint, sharper reviewers, packaging), placed the board, kit, siblings, retrieval, canon editor and drift trial in Full, and excluded automated posting, idea feeds, canon serving other tools and learning from edits.

dimensions.label: Consistency
dimensions.evidence: Six tensions with earlier contracts (self-repair vs protected prose, retrieval vs frozen inputs, archive exemplars vs the no-archive-anecdote rule, kit claims, Vale vs native PHP, sibling gates) were resolved in writing, lint blocking and drag semantics were decided explicitly, and critic blockers on SQLite vectors and canon propagation were fixed and recorded.

problem: The owner wants every Birdcar post to sound like him and to serve the same business goals: owners of established service businesses as the reader, one plain Walkthrough invitation, the outcome chain, and the claims and exclusion rules. Today the publishing workflow asks him to tick voice samples from previous posts for each article, and that mechanism barely works. Excerpts are cut to about 220 characters before the 1,200-character cap applies. The dashboard Develop path starts the interview with only the idea, so research, plan, draft and the automatic reviews receive an empty voice_context. No agent instruction tells a role how to use the samples. None of his style guide, public register, blog channel rules, narrative frameworks or PRODUCT.md positioning reaches any prompt, and BuyerReviewer is told not to invent buyer facts without being told who the buyer is.

The result is that voice and goals vary per post and the owner catches drift by hand. The pipeline also has structural gaps for producing marketable output: the raw idea becomes the article's slug and fallback title instead of a working summary with the real title set later as metadata; one idea can produce exactly one manuscript, with no distribution kit or sibling posts; the Planner has no notion of post type or narrative framework; mechanical rules such as the em dash ban, banned vocabulary, title and meta lengths and the single /walkthrough link are left to LLM attention; and there is no board showing where each piece sits across stages.

The owner's voice profile already exists in unusual detail (bat-kol style.md, registers/public.md, channels/blog.md, the new-post framework library and the marketingskills and Hormozi distillations), and the ten-agent pipeline with human angle, plan and release gates already exists. The work is to decompose that profile into what each role needs, freeze it into every activity, enforce what is mechanical deterministically, and refine the existing pipeline's stages so one idea reliably becomes several on-voice, on-goal pieces.
goals: G1 Inputs: every editorial activity kind freezes the active canon's version id and content hash, its own role rubric and the shared goals block into its input; Drafter and VoiceReviewer also receive the fixed exemplar canon labeled voice-only, and for blog pieces 2-4 retrieved exemplar sections; the per-post voice sample checklist no longer exists.

G2 Mechanical rules: every mechanical rule tagged in the canon has exactly one deterministic lint rule with a seeded-violation fixture that fires and a clean fixture that does not, every lint rule is tagged in the canon and stated in the Drafter's instructions, and title, SEO title, meta and slug rules are enforced once and shared by packaging and release.

G3 Drift detection: on a golden set of 10 real canon or site-copy passages and 10 slopped variants of the same passages, lint plus VoiceReviewer flag at least 9 of 10 distinct slopped passages at the injected span and raise a drift finding on no more than 2 of 10 distinct real ones, measured against the current canon hash.

G4 Pieces: one idea yields a flagship blog post plus LinkedIn, Bluesky and email pieces and any number of owner-requested sibling posts, each its own card with its own stage; the idea's summary title never becomes a piece's title or slug, and the real title and slug are set at packaging.
G5 Owner acceptance: the owner runs three real ideas end to end and judges each flagship and its kit publishable with light edits.
G6 Baseline: the edit distance between each agent-authored revision and the owner's next saved revision is recorded per piece, as a measured baseline with no target.

G7 Structure: every plan records a post type, a primary narrative framework from the blog channel's allowed list for that type and a runner-up with reasons, and the Drafter receives the chosen framework file in full.

G8 Canon ownership: the owner can change the canon in Admin without a deploy, the next activity freezes the new version, and a downloaded export committed to the repo keeps fresh environments and tests in step.

decisions.decision: One idea owns many pieces: a flagship blog post, LinkedIn, Bluesky and email kit pieces, and owner-requested sibling blog posts, each with its own stage
decisions.rejected: A flagship plus kit only, or sibling posts only; and the 2026-09-22 contract's exclusion of derivative generation
decisions.reason: The owner's end goal is one idea becoming potentially several marketable pieces

decisions.decision: Keep Article as the piece model with a kind and parent link, and add a ContentIdea model that owns the summary title
decisions.rejected: Renaming Article to a new Piece model
decisions.reason: Reuses revisions, releases, attempts and their tests; the rename would churn every publishing file for no behavior change

decisions.decision: Decompose bat-kol into repo-owned per-role rubric files as canon version 1; Admin-edited database versions win once the editor exists; a download of the active version is committed back to the repo
decisions.rejected: Syncing from bat-kol by heading manifest, the repo always winning, or Admin-only storage after import
decisions.reason: Production cannot read ~/.config, role decomposition is the point, and the owner wants the app's canon to eventually replace bat-kol

decisions.decision: A fixed exemplar canon of four 2026 essays plus approved site copy, with 2-4 sections retrieved per blog brief by the SDK's built-in embeddings from non-canon archive essays and pipeline-published pieces
decisions.rejected: A fixed canon only; per-post picking; the 2026-09-22 contract's rejection of an embeddings index; and indexing the canon essays and site copy already frozen in full
decisions.reason: The owner chose canon plus retrieval and noted the earlier avoidance of built-in embeddings had to be fixed afterward; the over-engineering critic showed indexing frozen material retrieves what every input already holds

decisions.decision: Embeddings use a dedicated openai-compatible provider entry keyed to the OpenRouter key and base URL, with openai/text-embedding-3-small at 1536 dimensions, set as the embeddings default; vector queries always receive precomputed embeddings
decisions.rejected: OpenAI direct or Gemini embeddings, and the shipped default_for_embeddings of openai
decisions.reason: Keeps OpenRouter as the only key and spending authority, as the 2026-09-24 contract decided; passing raw strings would silently embed through the default provider

decisions.decision: Several reviewers: keep the three lenses with sharper, distinct role rubrics, plus deterministic lint ahead of them
decisions.rejected: One general reviewer, or blogbot's single agent with one advisory critic
decisions.reason: Mechanical, judgment and reconciliation checks fail differently; research supports decomposed criteria and external grounding over one holistic critic

decisions.decision: Refine the existing stages: add an Ideas column, lint with at most two self-repair passes, a packaging step and kit pieces spawned at release approval; keep every current stage and gate
decisions.rejected: Merging research into planning, or dropping the angle gate
decisions.reason: The owner wants the pipeline refined into a seamless workflow, not replaced

decisions.decision: Packaging runs as a Packager activity whose metadata goes through the existing proposal-acceptance path, with metadata rules implemented once as lint rules that CheckArticleRelease enforces
decisions.rejected: A separate accepted-package gate and a new EditorialStage value, with the length rules validated twice (the pre-critic plan)
decisions.reason: The over-engineering critic showed CheckArticleRelease and metadata proposal acceptance already guard these fields; the owner's Package step survives as an activity on the board

decisions.decision: Deterministic lint findings block release unless each is overridden with a recorded reason; LLM style findings stay advisory
decisions.rejected: Lint as advisory only, matching the 2026-09-22 decision exactly, or a hard block with no override
decisions.reason: Mechanical rules like the em dash ban are absolute in the voice profile, but quoted sources can legitimately contain a banned word

decisions.decision: Implement the linter as native PHP rules, with every mechanical canon rule tagged by id and checked against registered lint rules in both directions
decisions.rejected: Vale, and a lint dataset that only lists implemented rules
decisions.reason: No external binary or dependency; the two-way id check means a canon rule cannot silently lack enforcement

decisions.decision: Self-repair rewrites only agent-authored blocks; owner-edited blocks get findings with proposed patches that are never auto-applied
decisions.reason: Preserves the 2026-09-22 rule that agents never silently change the owner's prose

decisions.decision: Release approval freezes the flagship's approved claim manifest; kit pieces are drafted from the approved flagship, may not add claims outside that manifest, and can be marked Posted only after the flagship is Published
decisions.reason: Keeps facts tied to checked claims and follows the blog channel rule against linking a post before it is published; the hidden-dependency critic found no claim-set artifact existed

decisions.decision: The Planner selects a primary narrative framework and a runner-up from the blog channel's allowed list for the post type; the owner chooses at the plan gate; PHP validates the allowed list and length exclusions
decisions.rejected: Leaving structure implicit in the outline, or scoring with framework-guide's topic tables as written
decisions.reason: Mirrors bat-kol's top-two selection; the topic tables were tuned for the old practitioner audience and the channel's per-type list supersedes them

decisions.decision: Board columns follow stage; drags are allowed only for single human actions; crossing a gate opens the workspace
decisions.rejected: Dragging across a gate approves it, or a read-only board
decisions.reason: The owner should approve the angle, plan and exact release text where he can read them

decisions.decision: Measure drift with 10 real and 10 slopped passages, passing at 9 of 10 caught and at most 2 of 10 real flagged, recomputed from recorded attempts and pinned to the current canon hash
decisions.rejected: A pairwise which-is-Nick judge, owner acceptance alone, or trusting the harness's own summary fields
decisions.reason: Tests the pipeline's own checks and goes stale automatically when the canon changes

decisions.decision: The MVP is the data model, canon, frameworks, lint, sharper reviewers and packaging; the board, kit, siblings, retrieval, canon editor and drift trial are Full
decisions.rejected: Everything as MVP, or the board first
decisions.reason: Owner choice; voice and goals consistency is the core and the board is a view over stages that must exist first

decisions.decision: The whole test suite moves from SQLite in memory to Postgres: birdcar_test on Herd locally (same host and port as development) and a pgvector-enabled Postgres service in CI; the vector migration calls Schema::ensureVectorExtensionExists() with no driver guard; the drift trial uses the same database
decisions.rejected: One retrieval test on the SQLite suite with embeddings faked (the pre-critic plan), a pgsql-guarded vector migration with only the vector tests on Postgres (the critic-fix plan), or a PHP-side similarity fallback
decisions.reason: Both the hidden-dependency and success-criteria critics showed SQLite throws on vector columns; the owner chose production parity over keeping the suite on SQLite

decisions.decision: Canon version 1 in Phases 2-7 is the repo files frozen by sha256 manifest hash; database versions, the Admin editor and a deploy-time sync arrive in Phase 8 after every rubric exists, deduplicating by hash and auto-activating a repo version only when the active version is the previous repo-sourced one
decisions.rejected: Seeding immutable database versions in Phase 2 (the pre-critic plan), which would strand the Phase 4 and Phase 6 rubrics outside already-seeded environments
decisions.reason: The hidden-dependency critic showed no path carried later rubrics into existing environments, and the over-engineering critic showed a versions table with one unchangeable row does no work before the editor exists

execution.strategy: Hybrid (artifacts generated; execution waits for the owner): a sequential spine (pieces, canon, lint, frameworks with reviewers and packaging) followed by Full-tier phases that branch off it, then a human acceptance gate. Commits go directly on main with linear history and no isolation branch; push only when the owner asks. Agent work stays queued and quality beats latency, so token limits and timeouts are runaway guards. Every phase that adds or changes an agent role runs a validator-to-schema audit and keeps EditorialInputContractTest green over EditorialActivityKind::cases(). The paid drift trial and the exemplar backfill never run automatically.
